title: Kioxia CM9-R 15.36TB E3.S NVMe SSD Review
gist: ServeTheHome begins reviewing Kioxia's CM9-R 15.36TB E3.S PCIe Gen5 NVMe SSD (BiCS8 TLC, dual-port capable, 1 DWPD), noting that 15TB-class drives now count as midrange in an era of 245/256TB-class SSDs; this excerpt covers specs only, not test results.

insights.claim: With 245/256TB-class SSDs now available, a 15.36TB enterprise drive is effectively midrange or even lower capacity.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Rapid capacity scaling in QLC/high-density SSDs is redefining tiers, pressuring HDD and mid-capacity SSD pricing.
insights.quote: now that we are in the era of 245/256TB-class SSDs, it is where we are

insights.claim: The Kioxia CM9-R 15.36TB E3.S uses BiCS FLASH generation 8 TLC on PCIe 5.0/NVMe 2.0, rated up to 14,800/11,000 MB/s sequential read/write and 3.4M/540K random 4K IOPS, with 1 DWPD endurance and a five-year warranty.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Gen5 TLC drives are saturating ~15GB/s reads, relevant for AI data pipelines and storage arrays.

insights.claim: Kioxia's CMx series targets enterprise high-availability arrays, supporting PCIe Gen5 in single x4 or dual x2 port modes.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Dual-port support positions CM9 for storage-array OEMs rather than hyperscale single-path servers.
insights.quote: With its CMx series of drives, Kioxia usually targets enterprise deployments where dual-port operation is important for high-availability arrays.

insights.claim: Compared with the 7.68TB CD9P-R previously tested, the CM9-R is expected to deliver similar reads but better write speeds.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Kioxia differentiates its CM (enterprise) and CD (data center) lines mainly on write performance and dual-port features.
insights.quote: we expect similar read speeds, but the CM9-R should offer better write speeds
